summary: Tested only the new DELETE /api/auth/account endpoint (ZedPulse v1.1 polish). Created /app/backend/tests/test_10_delete_account.py with 3 tests covering: (1) 401 without Bearer, (2) 401 with invalid Bearer, (3) full soft-delete flow — seeded a user with glucose+bp+medication+reminder+share_link+emergency_contact, called DELETE, then verified via API and direct MongoDB reads. All 3 tests pass. Did NOT re-run the 93 pre-existing tests as instructed.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:549 — GET /api/reminders does not filter by {deleted_at: {$exists: False}} like glucose/bp/medications do. Not exploitable after account delete (token is invalidated), but inconsistent with other soft-deleted collections. Low priority consistency fix.
server.py:167 — delete_account is not idempotent-safe: a second call with an already-invalid token will 401 (fine), but no explicit 'already deleted' handling. Current behaviour is acceptable.
seed_data_creation: Each test run creates one fresh TEST_DelAcctUser via signup, seeds 1 glucose + 1 bp + 1 medication + 1 reminder + 1 share_link + 1 emergency_contact, then soft-deletes it. A second fresh signup reclaims the phone number. All data is TEST_-prefixed; soft-deleted docs remain in DB with deleted_at set (per data_management_rules).
context_for_next_testing_agent: DELETE /api/auth/account verified end-to-end on https://vitals-monitor-105.preview.emergentagent.com. Soft-delete semantics confirmed at DB level: users.deleted_at set + phone renamed to deleted-{id}; glucose/bp/medications/reminders all have deleted_at set and docs remain; share_links.revoked=true (public /api/share/{token} => 404); emergency_contacts hard-deleted. Same token after delete => /auth/me 401, login with old phone+passcode => 401, fresh signup with same phone => 200.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found. Minor test authoring hiccup: initial reminder payload used 'title' (test_09 convention) instead of required 'label' (ReminderIn schema at server.py:540). Fixed in test file; endpoint itself is correct.
